title: BOOK THREE / CHAPTER ONE. On man, as he can be subjected to God and beatified, in common
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): BOOK THREE. Concerning ye subject, namely man, insofar as he stands as citizen belonging toward ye kingdom belonging toward God, capable belonging toward ye right plus life belonging toward God plus belonging toward eternal salvation. CHAPTER ONE. Concerning man, as he is able toward God to be subjected plus beatified, in common. Up to this point there was ye first thing, concerning which ye common part belonging toward sacred Theology acts, namely ye end belonging toward man absolutely highest plus last: there follows ye other, namely ye subject, which is man, insofar as he is able as citizen toward God his eternal king, by whom he was created plus redeemed, to be subjected, to be united, forever to be beatified, plus his highest end to attain.
pass_b_english: BOOK THREE. On the subject, namely man, insofar as he is a citizen of the kingdom of God, capable of the right and life of God and of eternal salvation.
CHAPTER ONE. On man, as he can be subjected to God and beatified, in common.

Thus far there has been the first thing treated by the common part of sacred Theology, namely the absolutely highest and last end of man: there follows the second, namely the subject, which is man, insofar as he can, as a citizen, be subjected to God his eternal King, by whom he was created and redeemed, be united to Him, be beatified forever, and attain his highest end.
source_text: LIBER TERTIUS, De subjecto, nempe homine, qua ut civis regni Dei, juris, vitaeque Dei & salutis aeternae capax est. CAPUT PRIMUM, De homine, qua Deo subjici & beari potest, communiter. Adhuc fuit primum, de quo agit sacrae Theologiae pars communis, nempe finis hominis absolute summus & ultimus: Sequitur alterum, subjectum videlicet, quod est homo, quatenus potest tanquam civis Deo aeterno regi suo, a quo conditus et redemtus est, subjici, uniri, aeternum beari, summumque finem suum adipisci.
